fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker visible from the street at the driveway entrance.
• Mark the detached structure with a visible identifier so responders can distinguish it from the main residence during an emergency response.
• Trim vegetation along the driveway edges to keep the path clear for emergency vehicle access.
• Clear overhanging branches or shrubs that may block a fire or rescue vehicle from reaching the detached structure.
• Post the secondary structure's location on any address signage or gate entry so responders are aware of multiple buildings on arrival.
• Keep at least one gate or opening in the perimeter fencing unlocked and clearly marked for emergency access.
• Thin dense vegetation between the main residence and the detached structure so responders can move between the two buildings without obstruction.
• Confirm the vehicle parking area does not block the path between the street and either structure during an emergency.
• Mark any locked fence gates with a Knox Box or coded lock system coordinated with your local fire department to allow rapid entry without forcing entry.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim branches on large trees that hang close to or over the structure.
• Thin the tree cluster nearest to the structure to create open space between individual trees.
• Remove shrubs growing directly against or immediately next to the structure.
• Keep the area between scattered shrubs and the structure clear of dead leaves and plant debris.
• Separate any shrubs growing beneath large trees so fire cannot move from the ground up into the tree canopy.
• Cut back low-hanging branches on scattered trees to reduce the path fire can take from ground vegetation up into the trees.
• Keep both access routes clear of overhanging branches and encroaching vegetation.
• Mow or clear dry grass and low vegetation in the open terrain areas close to the structure.
